Title: Senior Program Manager
Description:
**About Citco**

Citco is a global leader in fund services, corporate governance and related asset services, delivering end-to-end solutions and service to clients across its global organization.

**Role Purpose**

The Senior Program Manager is accountable for the strategic direction, integrated planning and end-to-end delivery performance of AXI within the Investor Relations Value Stream. In addition to the official Senior Program Manager title, the role fulfils the Value Stream Delivery Lead responsibilities for Investor Relations, ensuring that agreed outcomes and priorities are translated into a coherent roadmap, single governed backlog and measurable delivery plan.

As a member of the Investor Relations Value Stream Leadership Team, the role partners with the Value Lead, Technology Lead and Operations Lead to connect strategy with execution. The Senior Program Manager owns the overall flow and coordination of delivery, providing clear visibility of progress, capacity, cost, dependencies, risks, impediments and outcomes across AXI and related work.

As a Grade 4 leader, the Senior Program Manager operates with a high degree of autonomy and organizational influence. The role shapes delivery strategy, challenges constructively, resolves complex cross-functional constraints and represents the Value Stream in portfolio and executive forums. The position also includes formal line-management responsibility for staff within the Project Management Department, combining Value Stream delivery accountability with people leadership and capability development.

  

**Key Responsibilities**

Investor Relations Value Stream and AXI Delivery Leadership

* Fulfil the Delivery Lead role within the Investor Relations Value Stream Leadership Team, partnering with the Value Lead, Technology Lead and Operations Lead to turn agreed outcomes and priorities into executable delivery commitments.

* Own the integrated Investor Relations Value Stream roadmap, AXI program plan, single backlog and delivery performance, ensuring investment and execution remain aligned to agreed strategic objectives and measurable business outcomes.

* Lead a complex portfolio of projects and workstreams, balancing platform development, business change, operational readiness, releases and production priorities.

* Translate strategic direction and business cases into sequenced, achievable delivery plans with clear ownership, dependencies, milestones and success measures.
* Provide direction across cross-functional and globally distributed teams, creating alignment, pace, transparency, and accountability.
* Anticipate material delivery challenges and establish practical mitigation, recovery or escalation strategies before outcomes are affected.
* Act as the senior delivery authority for AXI and the Delivery Lead for the Investor Relations Value Stream, representing delivery in Value Stream, portfolio, executive and governance forums.
* Drive consistent delivery practices, delivery metrics and continuous improvement while allowing teams to apply fit-for-purpose Agile, Waterfall or hybrid methods.
* Coordinate cross-Value Stream demand and dependencies, negotiate sequencing with shared services and escalate priority decisions where demand exceeds available capacity.
* Manage Value Stream capacity, resource demand and allocation, ensuring commitments are realistic and delivery constraints are visible early.
* Lead quarterly planning, roadmap reviews, execution reviews and delivery governance across strategic change, client work, business requests, platform change and KTLO activity.
* Maintain one visible and prioritized backlog linking Value Stream outcomes and objectives to executable epics, stories and delivery commitments, with clear ownership and no orphaned work.
Establish and facilitate the regular Investor Relations Value Stream leadership cadence, ensuring shared ownership across value, delivery, technology and operations.  

**Value Stream Delivery, Flow and Ways of Working**

Integrated Planning, Governance and Financial Control

* Develop and maintain integrated Value Stream plans, roadmaps, budgets, forecasts, capacity and resource plans, and delivery scenarios across AXI and related Investor Relations outcomes.
* Establish proportionate governance across the full delivery lifecycle, including business case, scope, schedule, financials, quality, RAID, decisions, dependencies and benefits.
* Ensure program commitments are realistic and supported by sufficient capacity, funding, technical readiness and business ownership.
* Lead Value Stream prioritization and trade-off discussions where demand exceeds capacity or where scope, sequencing, cost, dependencies or risk require leadership or executive decision.
* Provide concise, evidence-based reporting on delivery confidence, financial position, outcomes and material constraints.
* Ensure program delivery complies with applicable Project Management Department, PMO, SDLC, risk and control requirements

**Technology Delivery and Release Oversight**

* Oversee delivery across the SDLC, ensuring requirements, design, engineering, testing, UAT, performance, release and production-readiness activities are integrated and governed.
* Partner with product, business and technology leadership to maintain alignment between business outcomes, platform priorities and technical execution.
* Coordinate cross-platform, cross-program and cross-Value Stream dependencies, ensuring demand, blockers and integration risks are visible, owned, sequenced and resolved.
* Ensure releases have clear acceptance criteria, quality evidence, operational readiness, communications, implementation and support arrangements.
* Own the health of the Value Stream delivery system, using flow, quality, capacity and financial data to identify bottlenecks, remove impediments, improve predictability and support continuous improvement.
Promote fit-for-purpose use of Agile, Waterfall and hybrid approaches rather than applying a single methodology by default.  

**Executive and Stakeholder Leadership**

* Build trusted relationships with executive sponsors, business leaders, technology leaders, operations, control functions and external partners.
* Communicate complex delivery matters clearly and directly, adapting detail and recommendations to the audience.
* Present program status, risks, dependencies, investment choices and strategic recommendations to senior governance forums.
* Create a consistent program narrative across stakeholders and ensure decisions, commitments and accountabilities are understood and followed through.
* Challenge constructively where delivery confidence, scope, sequencing, ownership or expected value is unclear.
* Navigate competing priorities and organizational complexity while protecting agreed program outcomes.

**People Leadership and Project Management Capability**

* Provide formal line management for assigned staff within the Project Management Department, including regular one-to-ones, objective setting, performance and development conversations, and support for career growth.
* Set clear expectations for delivery quality, professional conduct, stakeholder management, governance and accountability.
* Allocate and balance work across direct reports, considering program priorities, individual capability, development needs and sustainable workload.
* Coach and mentor project and program management professionals, providing practical guidance on complex delivery situations and supporting sound judgement.
* Identify capability, capacity and succession needs within the team and contribute to recruitment, onboarding, talent development and retention.
* Promote consistent standards, reusable practices and knowledge-sharing across the Project Management Department and relevant communities of practice.
* Create an inclusive, collaborative environment where staff receive timely feedback, understand priorities and are supported to perform effectively.

**Measures of Success**

* Investor Relations Value Stream priorities and AXI investment are translated into one realistic, governed and outcome-focused roadmap and backlog.
* Program commitments are delivered with clear ownership, executive visibility and effective financial control.
* Material risks and dependencies are identified early, with timely decisions and credible mitigation or recovery plans.
* Business, product and technology stakeholders remain aligned on priorities, sequencing, delivery confidence and expected outcomes.
* Releases are delivered with appropriate quality, operational readiness and production support.
* Project Management Department staff have clear objectives, balanced assignments, regular feedback and meaningful development support.
* The Investor Relations Value Stream and AXI delivery teams demonstrate improving flow, predictability, transparency, collaboration and measurable value.

  

**Knowledge, Skills and Experience**

Essential

* Extensive experience leading large, complex and strategically important technology programs across multiple projects, workstreams and stakeholder groups.
* Demonstrated experience owning delivery execution, flow, planning, capacity, dependencies and governance within a Value Stream, product or comparable cross-functional operating model.
* Proven accountability for end-to-end program delivery, including strategy translation, integrated planning, governance, financial control, risk, dependency, quality and executive reporting.
* Demonstrated ability to operate autonomously, influence senior leaders and make sound decisions in ambiguous or high-pressure situations.
* Strong experience coordinating delivery across business, product, engineering, architecture, testing, operations and control functions.
* Deep understanding of SDLC and delivery methods, including Agile, Waterfall and hybrid approaches, with the judgement to tailor governance appropriately.
* Proven people-management experience, including objective setting, coaching, performance management, development planning, workload management and recruitment support.
* Experience leading and developing project or program management professionals across distributed teams.
* Excellent executive communication, facilitation, negotiation and influencing capability.
* Strong commercial and financial acumen, including budget management, forecasting, resource planning and investment trade-offs.
* Ability to connect program outputs to business outcomes, adoption and measurable value realization.

Desirable

**Personal Attributes**

* Strategic and outcome-focused, while remaining close enough to execution to intervene effectively.
* Creible and composed with senior stakeholders in complex or high-stakes situations.
* Decisive, pragmatic and willing to make delivery issues visible.
* Strong ownership mindset with high personal accountability.
* Inclusive people leader who sets clear expectations and invests in the development of others.
* Collaborative and able to lead through influence across organizational boundaries.
* Resilient, adaptable and committed to continuous improvement.

**Role Accountabilities**

The Senior Program Manager fulfils the Delivery Lead role for the Investor Relations Value Stream and owns delivery execution, flow, integrated planning, governance, financial control, dependencies and delivery performance for AXI. The Value Lead remains accountable for value, vision and priority decisions; the Technology Lead remains accountable for architecture, engineering quality and technical direction; and the Operations Lead remains accountable for operational input, readiness and adoption. The Senior Program Manager brings these perspectives together into one executable delivery system and is accountable for the effective line management and development of assigned Project Management Department staff.

**Our Benefits**

Your well-being is of paramount importance to us and central to our success. We provide a range of benefits, training and education support, and flexible working arrangements to help you achieve success in your career while balancing personal needs. Ask us about specific benefits in your location.

Citco recognizes diversity as a source of organizational pride and strength. Citco welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities, and accommodations are available upon request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process.

Title: Director of Business Technology
Description:
Liteline Corporation is a privately held Canadian commercial lighting manufacturer with more than 160 employees, selling across Canada and the United States. We are adding a Director of Business Technology to our leadership team, a senior, hands-on role with ownership of technology across the business.

The role has two halves. The first is the job every growing company needs: keep our technology running, secure and recoverable across roughly 130 computers, Microsoft 365, our server cluster and our network. The second is newer. Our own people, from the three Co-Presidents to staff in Finance, Product Development, Engineering and Customer Service, now build software tools with AI assistants. The Director of Business Technology will give that work a professional backbone: version control, permissions, backups and fast recovery.

This is an enabling role as much as a technical one. We want our people to keep building quickly. The person in this position will make sure what they build is safe, recoverable and well looked after, without slowing anyone down.

This is a build role. Liteline’s people are already creating their own tools with AI. We are looking for a leader who can keep the core IT environment solid, put the right platforms and guardrails under home-built software, and teach non-programmers to work safely.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Keep Things Running**

* Own day-to-day IT across the business: computers, email, servers, networking, security and backups.
* Run Microsoft 365, including sign-in, multi-factor authentication (MFA), user access and licensing.
* Look after our on-premises server cluster, storage and network infrastructure.
* Oversee security monitoring and incident response together with our security monitoring partner.
* Maintain tested backups and the ability to restore systems and data quickly.
* Lead the help desk and set the service standards the business is held to.

**Own the Platforms**

* Set up and run, hands-on, the platforms our home-built tools live on.
* Own Liteline’s company GitHub organization, where code is saved with full history, including structure, permissions, single sign-on (SSO) and branch protection.
* Administer hosted databases (Supabase / Postgres), including access control, backups and recovery.
* Manage website and application hosting (Netlify), including deployments, domains and environments.
* Maintain a clear inventory of the tools in use, who owns each one and where it runs.

**Govern and Teach**

* Decide what AI assistants can access and set sensible guardrails for company data and credentials.
* Set light, practical rules that protect the business without getting in the way of the people building.
* Decide which home-built tools are business-critical and what level of protection each one needs.
* Run and rehearse restores so that recovery is proven, not assumed.
* Teach staff who are not programmers to work safely, for example explaining version control to someone in purchasing.
* Run training, enablement and “lunch and learn” sessions across the business.

**Team and Partners**

* Lead two on-site IT staff.
* Manage our outside partners for managed services, security monitoring and backup.
* Own the technology budget, licensing and vendor relationships, and bring forward stronger options as the market moves.

**WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR**

We are looking for a hands-on technology leader who is equally comfortable running core IT and building platforms that sit under modern, AI-assisted development.

The successful candidate will understand infrastructure, identity and security, and will also understand how software is built, saved, deployed and recovered. Just as importantly, you will be able to explain those ideas in plain language to people who have never written code and help them adopt habits that last.

**Strong candidates will bring:**

* Hands-on experience setting up or administering a GitHub organization, including SSO and branch protection.
* Experience running a Microsoft Power Platform Centre of Excellence, citizen-developer or low-code programme.
* Hands-on experience running Supabase, Postgres, Netlify, Vercel or similar platforms.
* Solid Microsoft 365, identity, MFA, endpoint and security fundamentals.
* A track record of training and enabling non-technical staff, such as “lunch and learn” or enablement programmes.
* Experience building a function or process from scratch at a growing company.
* Clear communication and sound judgment about when rules help and when they get in the way.

There is no single path to this role. You might be:

* An IT lead at a 100-to-500-person manufacturer or distributor who personally ran a Power Platform governance programme, a low-code programme or the company’s GitHub organization.
* A developer or DevOps engineer who moved into an IT management role at a small or mid-sized company.
* A solutions architect or senior consultant at a managed services provider (MSP) serving small and mid-sized businesses, ready to go in-house.
* The “first IT hire” at a startup who set up sign-in, devices and GitHub from scratch, then moved to a mid-sized company.
* Experience in mid-sized manufacturing, distribution or wholesale is helpful but not required.

**REPORTING AND WORKING RELATIONSHIPS**

This position reports to the VP of Operations.

You will work closely with Liteline’s three Co-Presidents, who are technically capable and build their own tools, and with Finance, Product Development, Engineering and Customer Service. You will be a partner to the people building, not a gatekeeper.

**LOCATION AND WORKING ARRANGEMENT**

This position is based at Liteline's Richmond Hill head office and is on-site five days per week with regular presence at our distribution facilities.

The successful candidate should expect to be highly engaged with the business and to spend real time understanding how departments and facilities actually operate.

**THE OPPORTUNITY**

This is a rare chance to shape how an established Canadian manufacturer builds and runs its technology at a moment when AI is changing who can create software.

Liteline is privately held, decisions are made without layers of approval, and good ideas get backed. Our leaders build with technology themselves and value this work. The Director of Business Technology will define the platforms, guardrails and habits that let the whole company build with confidence.

**WHAT WE OFFER**

Liteline offers a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental and life insurance following three months of service, and a group RRSP with partial company match.

**TO APPLY**

Qualified candidates are invited to apply directly through this posting.

*Liteline Corporation is an equal opportunity employer that values the unique skills and experiences of every candidate. We are committed to accommodating people with disabilities throughout the recruitment and hiring process. To request accommodation, please contact Human Resources with the position title in the subject line.*

Pay: $150,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* Company events
* Disability insurance
* Employee assistance program
* Extended health care
* Life insurance
* On-site parking
* RRSP match
* Vision care

Application question(s):

* How many years of work experience do you have with IT Strategy?
* Have you built or significantly developed an IT, business technology, technology governance, or technology enablement function or process from the ground up?
* Do you have hands-on experience setting up or administering a GitHub organization, including SSO, permissions, branch protection or repository governance?
* Do you have hands-on experience administering Microsoft 365 environments, including identity, MFA, endpoint management, and security?
* Do you have hands-on experience administering or supporting platforms such as Supabase, PostgreSQL, Netlify, Vercel, or similar technologies?

Experience:

* IT: 7 years (required)
* DevOps: 3 years (required)
* Microsoft Platform: 3 years (required)

Title: Manager, Care Operations
Description:
**Overview**
Tonal Care runs seven days a week across an in-house Toronto team and an outsourced partner operation. The Manager, Care Operations owns how that operation performs day to day.
  
  
You will own daily delivery across all tiers, the operational relationship with our outsourced partner, and the staffing and capacity plans that keep service levels intact. You will lead a Team Lead and a team of Customer Experience Specialists, each of whom owns one or two lines of business, and you will work the queue yourself when coverage requires it.
  
  
This is a hands-on, player/coach, operating role. You set the standard, work within it, and hold the operation to it.
  
  
What You Will Do
  
  
Daily Delivery
  
  

* Act as a player-coach during the initial phase, spending dedicated time working directly in the queue alongside specialists to model best practices, coach in real time, and establish baseline workflows
* Own daily delivery across all tiers, setting service levels, coverage models, and workflow standards that hold consistent delivery across phone, email, chat, and video.
* Own the daily, weekly, and monthly plans for SLA, CSAT, Average Handle Time, and First Contact Resolution, and be accountable for hitting them.
* Identify performance trends, operational risks, and root causes, and build the action plans that close the gap.
* Lead regular performance reviews and operational business reviews with internal stakeholders and partner leadership.
* Support incident and volume management during elevated contact periods, product issues, launches, and other business disruptions.
* Work the queue yourself when coverage requires it — absences, PTO, peak volume, or an uncovered line of business. You are the final backstop on coverage.
* Translate operational data into clear insights and recommendations for Care leadership.

Outsourced Partner Performance
  
  

* Serve as the day-to-day operational point of contact for Tonal’s outsourced partner, managing performance through their team leads and supervisors.
* Hold partner leadership accountable to agreed KPIs, SLAs, quality standards, staffing commitments, and Tonal’s brand voice.
* Run weekly performance reviews with partner teams.
* Report weekly to our Logistics, Field Operations, and Care Leadership team across all Care Operations metrics.
* Partner with their leadership on performance improvement plans, staffing strategies, coaching opportunities, and operational readiness.
* Monitor partner staffing, attrition, attendance, and utilization to catch capacity risk before it reaches Members.
* Make sure partner teams are aligned to Tonal policies, workflows, and operating standards, and are prepared for new programs, product changes, and launches.
* Escalate to the Senior Manager, Care Operations when partner performance issues cannot be resolved at the working level. Contract terms, rates, and renewals sit with the Director of Care Operations.

Staffing and Capacity
  
  

* Own workforce planning with partner Workforce Management and Tonal analytics, setting capacity and staffing models against forecast demand and adjusting intraday to protect service levels.
* Plan coverage across the full seven-day operating window, including weekends, holidays, and peak periods.
* Own the volume, staffing, and partner utilization assumptions that feed Care’s operating budget.
* Monitor forecast accuracy and adjust staffing assumptions based on actual contact volume, productivity, shrinkage, and service-level performance.
* Ensure schedules keep the teams at a sustainable working load rather than at full utilization, so there is room to absorb spikes and absences.

Team Leadership
  
  

* Lead and develop the team through the Team Lead and senior specialists, owning performance calibration, coaching, career development, and coverage planning.
* Make sure every line of business has a named owner, that the assignment is understood, and that owners are held to how their domain performs.
* Be accountable for the escalations programme. Specialists and the Team Lead resolve individual escalations; you own how the programme performs and where it needs to change.
* Sit in the health, safety, and legal escalation chain: Specialist → Team Lead → Manager, Care Operations → Senior Manager, Care Operations → Director, Care Operations.
* Ensure clear ownership and communication on sensitive, complex, or high-risk Member situations.
* Monitor escalation trends to surface recurring Member pain points, and work with the frontline to reduce avoidable escalations and lift first contact resolution.

Process and Partnership
  
  

* Translate the operating plan set with the Senior Manager, Care Operations into daily execution, and own that execution.
* Work with the Care Enablement team to identify knowledge gaps and roll out new troubleshooting SOPs, training, and tool updates to the front line.
* Coordinate with Logistics and Field Operations to deliver a seamless end-to-end experience for both specialists and Members.
* Simplify workflows to reduce Member effort, improve specialist efficiency, and remove unnecessary operational friction.
* Represent Care Operations in cross-functional initiatives and launches, and support the rollout and adoption of new tools, processes, and support programs.

Coverage and Schedule
  
  
Tonal Care operates seven days a week, 9:00 AM to 10:00 PM EST. This is a hands-on leadership role and the coverage expectations come with it:
  
  

* You and your team may be required to work weekends, holidays, and after hours as coverage requires. You and your team’s schedule will shift with the needs of the operation.
* Your team will carry on-call responsibility for incidents, outages, product issues, and elevated volume periods.
* Priorities change during the day. Peak season, launches, and product escalations will change what a day looks like.

Who You Are
  
  

* You have 5+ years of experience in Customer Care, Customer Support, or Contact Center Operations, including 2+ years leading teams, vendors, or outsourced operations.
* You are operationally minded and move comfortably between the operating plan and the queue. You set the standard, then hold the operation to it.
* You have managed operational KPIs and used data to find and fix performance problems. You don’t just report numbers — you understand the why behind them and change process, staffing, or enablement to move the trend.
* You are an empathetic coach who knows how to motivate a team and can turn complex data into feedback a specialist can act on.
* You have handled complex escalations and high-impact customer situations, and you are comfortable navigating gray areas and making quick, sound decisions when they arise.
* You have strong vendor and stakeholder management skills, and can influence partners who don’t report to you.
* You are technically savvy and proficient in CRM and support tooling, with an understanding of how backend systems shape the frontline experience.
* You prioritize influence over authority, earning the trust of your team and stakeholders to drive results through collaboration rather than mandate.
* You are comfortable operating in a fast-moving environment with changing priorities and evolving processes.

Why You Will Love Working at Tonal
  
  

* You will own the operating model for a Care organization that is scaling across channels and lines of business
* Competitive compensation package, benefits, and Tonal product perks
* Collaborative, mission-driven team with a passion for redefining strength training

At Tonal, we believe that the unique and varied lived experiences of our teammates contribute to our overall strength. We don’t just appreciate differences, we celebrate them, and we always seek people that represent a wide variety of backgrounds. We’re dedicated to adding new perspectives to the team and designing employee experiences that contribute to your growth as much as you do to ours. If your experience aligns with what we’re looking for (even if you don’t check every single box), send us your application. We would love to hear from you!
  
  
Tonal is committed to meeting the diverse needs of people with disabilities in a timely manner that is consistent with the principles of independence, dignity, integration, and equality of opportunity. Should you have any accommodation requests, please reach out to us via our confidential email, accessibility@tonal.com. All requests will be addressed and responded to in accordance with Tonal’s Accessibility Policy and local legislation.
  
  
Compensation Range: CA$95K - CA$120K

Title: Market Operations Manager
Description:
**Job Description:**  
What Youll Do
  
  
As the Market Operations Manager for Trü Frü Canada, you will own inventory planning, logistics, and supply chain execution for the Canadian market from end to end. This is a first-of-its-kind role built to unlock exponential growth. You will build the processes, tools, and partnerships needed to scale across our frozen (cold chain) and dried portfolios. You will ensure flawless product availability while protecting our gold-standard service levels.
  
  
Job Responsibilities
  
  

* Partner within the Canadian Market Unit to turn short-, medium-, and long-term sales targets into actionable operational plans.
* Work with the US demand team to keep forecasts highly accurate and aligned with commercial plans.
* Align with production and inventory planners to ensure timely manufacturing and cross-border transit. Proactively prevent service disruptions in the market.
* Represent Canadian interests in Steps 2 and 3 of the SOP process, as required.
* Direct logistics and 3PL partners to position inventory across Canada in support of short-term sales plans.
* Partner with Logistics to evaluate, select, and onboard new logistics providers.

Explore Mars network synergies for frozen and ambient (freeze-dried) supply chains.
  

* Manage retailer compliance (On-Time-In-Full, or OTIF) to protect service levels and minimize customer shortfalls. Reduce retail delivery fines and deductions.
* Give the sales team real-time inventory visibility. Work directly with retail partners on supply challenges, customer allocations, and creative delivery solutions.
* Diagnose process bottlenecks and reporting gaps. Design a dynamic, scalable, and self-serve operation for the Canadian Market Unit.
* Use AI and advanced data analytics to continuously monitor supply chain health, automate reporting, and generate predictive insights.

Qualifications
  
  

* University degree, preferably in business and/or supply chain.
* 7 years of progressive experience in demand, supply, inventory management, or logistics roles.
* Experience working directly with major Canadian retailers, including managing compliance and reducing fines.
* Experience partnering cross-functionally with internal teams.
* Experience designing and implementing operational processes.
* Ability to travel to the U.S. approximately 4 times a year for North American team meetings and trade shows.
* Travel within Canada for customer visits and trade shows (2–3 times a year), as required.

**Pluses:**  

* Cold chain experience
* Bilingual (English and French)

Title: Contact Center Manager
Description:
Trust is everything for financial institutions, but it gets harder to earn as customer expectations rise and fraud keeps evolving. At Casap, we’re on a mission to deliver outcomes that were once out of reach, building a future where fraud is rare and trust is a given.
  
  
We started with disputes, some of the highest-stakes work financial institutions can’t afford to get wrong, and have expanded the same approach across fraud, collections, claims and more. Today, more than 100 banks, credit unions, fintechs and processors trust our AI agents to make decisions, take actions, move money and file chargebacks, from first signal to final outcome.
  
  
Founded by product leaders from Robinhood and Chime, Casap has raised $90M, including a $56M Series B led by Base10 Partners with continued investment from Lightspeed and Emergence. We were named Tearsheet’s 2026 AI Company of the Year, and our CEO, Shanthi, was named to Inc.’s 2026 Female Founders 500. We have an exceptionally ambitious and kind culture, and we’re just getting started.
  
  
**Location(s)**
This is a hybrid role based out of our San Francisco, CA office. Our team works in-office time on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays.
  
  
**About The Role**
We're looking for a Contact Center Manager to join our Managed Services team and oversee our BPO operations day to day. As Managed Services expands, our BPO engagement is the compliant, reliable entry point for every fintech and credit union client we support. You'll lead our outsourced contact center and back-office investigation teams, manage policies and procedures, optimize IVR routing and call scripts, and turn vendor partnerships into clear results for our clients.
  
  
**What You'll Do**

* Own BPO Performance Day to Day: Serve as the primary operational contact for our contact center vendor(s). Manage SLA adherence, stand up performance reporting, run a regular vendor review cadence, and escalate underperformance with clear evidence and a path to resolution.
* Own IVR Design and Call Routing: Design, test, and optimize IVR flows and routing logic across vendor platforms. Reproduce routing issues, review call logs and data, and identify root cause before escalating to the vendor, engineering, or product.
* Own Scripting and Quality Standards: Partner with the QA/Performance Manager to build and maintain call scripts, quality standards, and calibration practices that keep every interaction compliant, consistent, and on-brand for each client.
* Partner on Workforce Management: Collaborate with WFM to align staffing, scheduling, and coverage planning with volume forecasts, and flag capacity risks before they affect clients.
* Own Security and Compliance for Phone Intake: Define and monitor controls for phone-based intake, including caller authentication and data handling. Audit the vendor against those controls and drive remediation of any gaps.
* Own Outcomes, Not Just Tickets: Treat recurring vendor or call-quality issues as programs to be solved. Define scope, align internal stakeholders and the vendor, and deliver durable resolutions rather than one-off fixes.
* Be the Bridge to Engineering and Product: Translate contact center and client friction into clear technical requirements and prioritized, business-context-rich input. Advocate for scalable solutions, including tooling integrations and automation.
* Optimize Contact Center Tooling: Partner with Managed Services Leadership on the integration and optimization of contact center platforms (e.g., TaskUs or equivalent).[C1]
* Support Client Relationships: Support the Vendor Ops Manager in client-facing work by providing performance data, preparing for business reviews, and connecting vendor results to each client’s operational goals.
* Drive Enablement and Documentation: Build the runbooks, escalation paths, and training materials that make the vendor self-sufficient and prevent repeat issues. Support the implementation team in standing up phone intake for new Managed Services clients.

**What You’ve Done**

* 4-7 years in contact center operations, vendor management, technical account management, or customer success, ideally at a B2B SaaS or fintech company serving financial institutions.
* Experience managing outsourced or in-house contact center operations at scale, ideally in a regulated industry, with hands-on IVR, WFM, and vendor SLA management.
* Experience in payments, disputes, chargebacks, or Reg E/Z compliance workflows, and familiarity with compliance requirements for phone-based financial services intake.
* A track record of turning vendor relationships into measurable, accountable performance.
* Ability to investigate issues independently: reviewing call data and logs, querying data, and identifying root cause before escalating.
* Strong relationship management skills, with the presence to build credibility with vendor leadership and with operational and executive stakeholders at clients.
* Exceptional written and verbal communication: able to make a complex operational or dispute issue clear to both frontline teams and leadership, and to work closely with QA, Product, and vendor partners.
* Structured problem-solver with great composure when an issue is live and the stakes are high, comfortable building process while doing the work in an early-stage environment.

**Compensation**
The base pay range for this role is $80,000 – $100,000 per year.
  
  
Casap's compensation package includes a competitive base salary benchmarked against real-time market data, as well as equity for all full-time roles. We also offer exceptional benefits, as well as bonuses and commission plans for applicable roles. The listed US-based compensation range is a guideline and may be modified. Final compensation will vary based on market conditions, geographic location, and candidate qualifications, including relevant knowledge, skills, and experience assessed during the interview process.
  
  

* 📈 Start-up equity

Title: Project Engineering Manager, Staff
Industry: Semiconductor Manufacturing, Software Development, and Computer Hardware Manufacturing
Description:
We Are
  
  
Synopsys is the leader in engineering solutions from silicon to systems, enabling customers to rapidly innovate AI-powered products. We deliver industry-leading silicon design, IP, simulation and analysis solutions, and design services. We partner closely with our customers across a wide range of industries to maximize their R&D capability and productivity, powering innovation today that ignites the ingenuity of tomorrow.
  
  
What You'll Be Doing
  
  

* Own and maintain the integrated schedule and critical path across multiple Memory Interface IP development and release workstreams, from project kickoff and architecture through design closure, verification, customer delivery, and production readiness. Model dependency chains deeply enough to quantify the impact of slips and pull-ins, distinguish paths with float from those without it, and update the plan weekly using current engineering data.
* Drive the weekly project cadence by synthesizing inputs from architecture, RTL, design verification, analog and mixed-signal design, physical design, packaging, software, infrastructure, product engineering, and post-silicon teams into a single view of program health, emerging concerns, and required actions.
* Track verification convergence and engineering maturity as leading indicators. Monitor feature readiness, RTL closure, bug discovery and closure trends, regression health, coverage, design maturity, and block-level readiness. Recognize when convergence is stalling and drive a recovery plan before downstream milestones or customer commitments are affected.
* Analyze schedule scenarios and coordinate recovery plans. Work with engineering leads to understand technical constraints, resource limitations, and available float; quantify the impact of changes; develop practical options; and track agreed recovery actions to closure.
* Manage external partner and customer dependencies by owning delivery calendars, tracking execution plans and acceptance criteria, aligning technical dependencies, and supporting schedule negotiations with a clear understanding of downstream technical, commercial, and resource impacts.
* Lead cross-functional risk, issue, and decision management. Convert technical uncertainty into clear options, owners, dates, and decision points. Ensure risks, assumptions, and trade-offs are visible early and resolved at the appropriate level.
* Provide concise project insight to executives and customers. Distill complex engineering information into evidence-based updates that distinguish signal from noise, quantify schedule and delivery impact, and clearly identify the actions or decisions needed.

A Day In The Life
  
  
You start the morning reviewing verification-convergence dashboards and regression results, spotting a block where bug-closure velocity has slowed. You bring the DV lead and RTL owner together for a focused sync, clarify the cause, and align on a recovery plan before the weekly project review.
  
  
In that review, you walk leadership through an updated critical path that reflects an internal delivery shift, quantify the downstream impact on release timing and customer commitments, and identify the decisions needed to protect the plan. Later, you follow-up with R&D on the strategy to take to resolve the issue, then finish the day preparing a concise executive summary and following up on owners and due dates from the project review.
  
  
What You'll Need
  
  

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Applied Science, Computer Science, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience, with 8+ years of relevant experience in semiconductor, silicon IP, SoC, ASIC, or complex hardware development.
* Demonstrated experience managing complex semiconductor or silicon IP programs across multiple engineering disciplines and geographically distributed teams.
* Strong working knowledge of semiconductor development lifecycles and the relationships among architecture, RTL, verification, analog and mixed-signal design, physical design, software, infrastructure, and productization.
* Demonstrated ability to build and maintain integrated schedules with meaningful dependency and critical-path modeling, including float analysis, milestone confidence, and the downstream effects of schedule changes.
* Experience using engineering evidence such as feature readiness, bug trends, regression results, coverage, design closure, and delivery health to assess schedule risk and drive corrective action.
* Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to evaluate complex technical and program information, develop practical options, and recommend a course of action.
* Strong communication and influence skills, including the ability to gain cooperation across engineering teams, customers, suppliers, and external partners and to present crisp status and recommendations to senior leadership.
* Experience with project and program management tools and data-driven reporting. Familiarity with Jira, schedule-management tools, dashboards, and engineering lifecycle metrics is preferred.
* Knowledge of quality-management processes and the ability to navigate Linux environments are considered assets.

Who You Are
  
  
This is not a status-reporting role. You will connect a broad set of engineering workstreams into a coherent, dependency-driven plan, identify the real critical path week to week, and drive the cross-functional actions and decisions that keep complex Memory Interface IP projects on track. The work spans concurrent development efforts with significant interdependencies across engineering disciplines, customers, external partners, and development infrastructure.
  
  
Working with general direction, you will apply strong semiconductor-development knowledge and program-management judgment to analyze issues, recommend practical solutions, and gain cooperation across teams. Success requires attention to engineering detail, disciplined follow-through, and the ability to turn complex technical inputs into clear priorities, ownership, and delivery commitments.
  
  
The Team You'll Be Part Of
  
  
Our engineering teams develop advanced Memory Interface IP that enables customers to build high-performance, differentiated SoCs. We work at the intersection of architecture, analog and mixed-signal design, RTL, verification, physical design, software, infrastructure, and customer deployment. The programs are technically complex, globally distributed, and tightly connected to customer and business commitments.
  
  
We value people who combine advanced technical judgment with clear communication, disciplined execution, and the willingness to work through details without losing sight of the broader outcome. In this role, you will help shape how complex semiconductor programs are planned and delivered, strengthen execution practices across teams, and work alongside talented engineers solving consequential problems at scale.
  
  
Rewards and Benefits
  
  
We offer a comprehensive range of health, wellness, and financial benefits to cater to your needs. Our total rewards include both monetary and non-monetary offerings. Your recruiter will provide more details about the salary range and benefits during the hiring process.
  
  
Synopsys Canada ULC values the diversity of our workforce. We are committed to provide access & opportunity to individuals with disabilities and will provide reasonable accommodation to individuals throughout the recruitment and employment process. Should you require an accommodation, please contact hr-help-canada@synopsys.com.

Title: Head of Information Technology
Description:
**Description:**

**Hybrid Role Monday - Friday 8:00AM-5:00PM**

The Head of Information Technology is the senior technology leader for Diagnostic Radiology and Imaging, LLC (DRI), accountable for translating business and clinical priorities into a secure, resilient, scalable, and service-oriented technology strategy. This role owns enterprise IT strategy, cybersecurity, infrastructure, clinical and business applications, data and integrations, vendor performance, IT financial management, disaster recovery, and technology governance across all DRI locations. This is a strategic leadership role with operational accountability. The Head of Information Technology builds and leads the IT function, establishes standards and measurable service levels, manages critical partners, and ensures that PACS, RIS, Microsoft 365, diagnostic workstations, modalities, interfaces, and supporting infrastructure reliably enable patient care and business operations.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**

**Enterprise Strategy and Executive Partnership**  

* Lead enterprise technology strategy, architecture, standards, policies, and investment priorities; maintain a multi-year roadmap and annual operating plan.
* Advise the executive leadership team on technology opportunities, risks, trade-offs, regulatory obligations, and the organizational impact of proposed initiatives.
* Partner with clinical, operations, finance, compliance, human resources, and affiliate leaders to define requirements, prioritize demand, and deliver solutions with measurable business outcomes.
* Establish IT governance, including intake, prioritization, change control, architecture review, project oversight, risk acceptance, and executive reporting.
* Perform technology due diligence and integration planning for new sites, affiliations, service lines, acquisitions, and major vendor changes.

**Cybersecurity, Privacy, Risk, and Compliance**  

* Maintain safeguards appropriate for protected health information and other confidential data.
* Maintain a current cybersecurity risk assessment and remediation roadmap; oversee identity and access management, privileged access, multifactor authentication, endpoint protection, vulnerability management, patching, logging, backup protection, email security, and network segmentation.
* Lead technology incident response and coordinate investigation, containment, recovery, communications, documentation, and post-incident improvements for security and operational events.
* Oversee third-party technology risk, security requirements, business associate obligations, evidence collection, audits, and corrective action plans.
* Ensure policies, procedures, access reviews, retention practices, workforce training, and technical controls support HIPAA, OSHA, contractual, and applicable regulatory requirements.

**Clinical Systems, Applications, and Integration**  

* Provide executive ownership for PACS, RIS, voice recognition, mammography reporting, advanced visualization, diagnostic workstations and monitors, modalities, interfaces, and other clinical systems supporting radiology operations.
* Ensure image availability, integrity, routing, presentation, reconciliation, and retention meet clinical, operational, and regulatory expectations.
* Oversee application lifecycle management, upgrades, testing, validation, change control, workflow design, training, optimization, and end-user adoption.
* Coordinate with modality, PACS, RIS, interface, and partner teams to troubleshoot complex cross-system issues and prevent recurrence.
* Develop governance for integrations, master data, interface monitoring, data quality, and controlled access to clinical and business information.

**Infrastructure, Cloud, and Service Delivery**  

* Own the reliability, security, capacity, and lifecycle of networks, connectivity, servers, cloud services, endpoints, printers, telephony, conference technology, Microsoft 365, and site technology.
* Implement a service management model with an accessible service desk, incident and problem management, asset and configuration management, knowledge articles, onboarding/offboarding controls, and measurable service levels.
* Establish availability, performance, capacity, patch, lifecycle, and technical-debt standards; plan replacements before systems reach unacceptable risk or end of support.
* Oversee installation and technology readiness for new and renovated sites, including connectivity, modality integration, workstation deployment, testing, cutover, and stabilization.
* Maintain tested backup, disaster recovery, business continuity, and clinical downtime capabilities; define recovery time and recovery point objectives with business owners and validate them through exercises.

**Financial, Vendor, and Portfolio Management**  

* Develop and manage the annual IT operating and capital budgets, forecast multi-year investments, and provide transparent variance and value reporting.
* Lead vendor selection, contracting, licensing, renewals, performance management, escalation, and exit planning in partnership with Finance, Legal, Compliance, and business owners.
* Rationalize applications, infrastructure, support agreements, and licensing to reduce unnecessary cost and complexity while preserving clinical quality and resilience.
* Build disciplined project and portfolio practices covering business cases, scope, resources, dependencies, risks, testing, change management, implementation, and benefit realization.
* Negotiate clear service levels, security obligations, implementation commitments, data ownership, support expectations, and business continuity provisions with key partners.

**People Leadership and Culture**  

* Design the IT organization and sourcing model; recruit, develop, coach, and retain technical talent and establish on call and escalation coverage appropriate to DRI operations.
* Set clear objectives and performance expectations, conduct regular one-on-ones and development planning, and hold employees and partners accountable for results and professional service.
* Promote a culture of ownership, documentation, collaboration, respectful communication, patient focus, and continuous learning.
* Communicate planned changes, incidents, risks, and service status clearly to executives, clinicians, staff, vendors, and affiliates.
* Perform other duties and lead other technology initiatives as assigned.

**Required Qualifications**  

* Bachelor’s degree in information technology, computer science, cybersecurity, healthcare administration, business, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and progressively responsible experience.
* Ten or more years of progressive information technology experience, including at least five years leading IT teams, vendors, budgets, and complex technology programs.
* Demonstrated success leading technology in a healthcare environment with responsibility for systems that support clinical operations and protected health information.
* Broad working knowledge of enterprise infrastructure, networking, cloud services, cybersecurity, identity and access management, end-user computing, service management, business continuity, application management, integrations, and data governance.
* Experience with radiology technology, including PACS and RIS, and with diagnostic workstations, modalities, interfaces, voice recognition, or related clinical imaging workflows.
* Experience managing Microsoft 365 and a Microsoft-based endpoint and identity environment.
* Proven ability to develop technology strategy, manage operating and capital budgets, negotiate with vendors, lead major incidents, and present effectively to executive leaders.
* Strong written and verbal communication, project leadership, analytical judgment, and change-management skills.

**Preferred Qualifications**  

* Master’s degree in information technology, cybersecurity, business administration, healthcare administration, or a related discipline.
* Relevant professional certification such as Certified Healthcare CIO (CHCIO), Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP), Certified Information Security Manager (CISM), Project Management Professional (PMP), or ITIL 4 certification.
* Experience supporting multi-site outpatient imaging, radiology practices, ambulatory healthcare, or physician enterprises.
* Experience developing cybersecurity capabilities using recognized healthcare and security frameworks and leading external assessments, audits, or remediation programs.
* Experience with mergers, acquisitions, new-site openings, major platform replacements, cloud migration, or clinical system modernization.

**Competencies**  

* Enterprise leadership and strategic thinking: Connects technology decisions to patient care, business outcomes, risk, and sustainable growth.
* Operational ownership: Creates clarity, follows through, measures results, and remains composed during high-impact incidents.
* Clinical and business partnership: Builds trust with clinicians, operators, executives, and external partners; translates effectively between technical and nontechnical audiences.
* Risk-based judgment: Makes timely, well-reasoned decisions while balancing security, reliability, usability, cost, and speed.
* Talent and vendor leadership: Develops internal capability and manages external partners as accountable extensions of the organization.
* Communication: Presents complex information, recommendations, and status in concise, decision-ready terms.

**Responsibility for Errors and Confidential Data**  
The role has high-level access to systems and confidential information, including protected health information. Failure to appropriately govern, secure, monitor, maintain, or recover technology may contribute to patient-care disruption, incorrect or unavailable patient data or images, privacy or security incidents, regulatory exposure, financial loss, and reputational harm. The Head of Information Technology is expected to exercise sound judgment, maintain confidentiality, and promptly escalate material risks and incidents.

**Physical Demands and Working Conditions**  
Work generally requires prolonged computer use, frequent communication, and periodic movement throughout office and remote work environments. The employee must be able to travel among DRI sites and occasionally access technology installed in work areas, equipment rooms, or near imaging operations. The position may periodically require after-hours availability for critical incidents, implementations, maintenance, or downtime exercises. The employee may occasionally need to transport a laptop, files, or technology equipment weighing up to approximately 50 pounds. Exposure to moving mechanical parts, electrical equipment, or radiology environments may occur when supporting site technology; required safety practices and personal protective equipment must be followed. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

**Conditions of Employment**  

* Compliance with DRI policies and all applicable privacy, security, safety, and regulatory requirements, including HIPAA and OSHA requirements.
* Ability to participate in an on-call or executive escalation structure and respond to critical technology events as business needs require.

Title: Training Program Manager, Security Operations

Powered by elite professionals from military, government, and intelligence backgrounds. If you are passionate about intelligence, risk analysis, threat management, executive protection, security operations, or business resiliency, Concentric may be the organization you've been searching for!  
  
Concentric is a risk consultancy specializing in delivering strategic security and intelligence services. We provide holistic, intelligent security solutions for private clients and corporations globally. Concentric offers strategic advisory services, risk assessments, physical protection, threat intelligence, open-source monitoring, program audits, secure embedded staffing, and training for security teams and intelligence analysts.  
  
Our ultimate goal is to be recognized as the most innovative, capable, and trusted Risk Management partner in the world, and we do this by following these core values:  
  
Integrity – Collaboration - Relationships – Excellence – Creativity - Results

Join Us,

Concentric - "Your World Secured"

We are currently seeking a Training Program Manager, Security Operations to join Concentric's Corporate Team.

This is a full-time, remote position. Days and hours of work are generally Monday through Friday. Evening and weekend work may be required to support training schedules for agents working varied shifts.

**IS THIS ROLE RIGHT FOR YOU?**

We're looking for an experienced executive protection professional who can both deliver training and run the program behind it.

You'll lead hands-on training for our embedded security teams, and over time for corporate employees. We have established courses in place, so you won't be starting from scratch, but you'll have the ownership to improve them and build new training where we have gaps. When we bring in outside vendors, you'll work alongside them and stay closely involved in delivery.

Just as important is the administrative side. You'll track licenses, certifications, and requalifications in tandem with our compliance team, schedule training around shift coverage and ongoing onboarding, and maintain audit-ready records for every agent. This role requires someone who is highly organized and detail-oriented. Strong instruction alone won't be enough to succeed here.

**JOB DESCRIPTION**

The Training Program Manager will deliver, manage, and continuously improve Concentric's training and certification program for Security Operations and physical security embedded positions, including armed and unarmed security personnel, executive protection agents, and residential security teams.

This is Concentric's first dedicated training role, created to support significant growth across our embedded client programs. The Training Program Manager will lead hands-on training for embedded security teams, with the opportunity to extend programs to Concentric's corporate employees. We have established courses, vendors, and a strong network in place, so this role is not a build from scratch. You'll have the ownership to improve existing training and create new courses where gaps exist.

Equally important, this role owns the administration that keeps the program running. You'll work in tandem with our compliance team to track licenses, certifications, and qualifications, schedule training around shift coverage and ongoing onboarding, and maintain complete, audit-ready records for every employee. You'll also serve as the company's subject matter resource on security training compliance, including California Bureau of Security and Investigative Services (BSIS) requirements and other evolving state and international regulations.

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

*Training Delivery & Development*

* Deliver hands-on training to embedded security personnel, with the opportunity to extend programs to Concentric's corporate employees

Title: Vice President of Product
Description:
**Job Summary**:

The Vice President of Product is accountable for the success of Tideworks' product portfolio: product strategy, roadmap priorities, customer adoption, product lifecycle management and the business outcomes delivered through Tideworks' products. The Vice President of Product owns what Tideworks builds and why. Reporting to the Chief Product & Technology Officer, the Vice President sets product strategy across the marine and intermodal rail portfolios, leads the product management organization  
(value stream managers, product managers, product owners, UX and data science), and runs the roadmap as a commitment to customers.

The role builds on deep product knowledge and long customer relationships and brings the product management discipline a growing software company needs: discovery with customers, design before build, business cases, competitive positioning and pricing. The VP sits on the product and technology leadership team and partners closely with the Chief Revenue Officer, Professional Services and Engineering. The first priority is modernizing the existing product suite while keeping customers successful, with AI, analytics and automation an explicit part of the product strategy.

The ideal candidate will possess deep knowledge of terminal operations and the software that runs them, a track record of building a product management practice, and executive presence with customers, partners and a board.

**JOB DESCRIPTION:**

**Product Strategy and Portfolio**  
● Own the product strategy and portfolio across marine and rail: where Tideworks invests, where it holds, and the long-term direction of the product suite  
● Define the product vision with the CPTO and bring it to the executive team and the board with the evidence behind it  
● Own competitive positioning and the market view that informs it  
● Own product investment priorities: propose where roadmap capacity and investment go, with a business case and an expected outcome for each, and report results in adoption, revenue, customer value and operational improvement  
● Identify new market opportunities and adjacent segments for the product suite

**Product Modernization**  
● Lead the modernization of the existing products: evolve the architecture with the CPTO and Engineering, sequence modernization against new capability, and balance innovation with technical debt reduction  
● Keep customers successful through the transition: upgrade paths, compatibility and clear communication of what changes and when

**AI, Analytics and Automation**  
● Make AI, analytics, optimization and automation an explicit part of the product strategy: where they create value in terminal operations, the data foundations they need, and proposals with business cases  
● Partner with Engineering on AI-assisted development so product decisions keep pace with faster delivery

**Product Management Organization**  
● Lead the product management organization: value stream managers, product managers, product owners, UX and data science  
● Set role expectations at each level, coach, hire and develop the team, and propose the structure needed to deliver the strategy  
● Run the product leadership cadence and represent product in company planning

**Product Management Discipline**  
● Establish customer discovery as standard practice, with product managers in front of terminal operators and their teams  
● Require end-to-end design with UX ahead of development, a clear definition of done, and a business case for every significant investment  
● Define the metrics that tell us a release worked and review them after every major release

**Roadmap and Planning**  
● Publish a roadmap cycle customers can plan around, and run customer advisory groups for marine and rail  
● Agree with Engineering the allocation of capacity between roadmap, maintenance and  
customer projects, and hold the line on it  
● Lead product’s part of quarterly planning with the development and quality engineering teams

**Platform and Architecture Partnership**  
● Set platform direction with the CPTO and architecture: extensibility and configurable  
workflows, a consistent API surface across products, and product behaviour that holds together across the suite  
● Put an architecture and design review in front of new capabilities and services

**Commercial Accountability and Partnership**  
● Own competitive positioning and win themes with the Chief Revenue Officer, and support RFP responses and gap analyses  
● Agree scope and packaging with Professional Services for implementations and upgrades  
● Bring pricing and packaging recommendations to the executive team  
● Share accountability with the Chief Revenue Officer for revenue growth, customer retention and expansion, and bring new market opportunities to the executive team

**Strategic Customer and Partner Relationships**  
● Build executive relationships with key customers, global terminal operators and partners  
alongside the Chief Revenue Officer, who owns the commercial relationship; help shape long-term opportunities and bring them into the portfolio

**Product Analytics and Customer Insight**  
● Instrument usage and adoption in the products and maintain a product view of customer  
satisfaction, and measure product success through adoption, revenue, customer value and  
operational improvements  
● Turn customer feedback, support themes and sales findings into prioritized product work

**Qualifications:**  
● Bachelor’s degree in Business, Engineering, Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent experience  
● 12+ years of enterprise software product management, including 6+ years leading product leaders (managers of product managers)  
● Domain experience in terminal operating systems or the industry around them: marine  
terminals, intermodal rail, port logistics; experience in both marine and rail strongly preferred  
● A track record of building a product management practice (discovery, design, pricing, roadmap) with the artifacts and results to show for it  
● Experience taking a mature, installed enterprise product through a modernization or platform transition while keeping customers successful  
● Executive presence with customers, partners and a board, and experience in a growth-investor environment  
● Technical fluency: APIs, data models, integration (EDI and messaging) and cloud deployment  
● Experience bringing AI, analytics or automation into an enterprise product  
● Executive relationships with terminal operators and industry partners  
● Leads through managers, sets clear expectations, decides on evidence, and has led teams across time zones  
● Preferred: Class 1 railroad or intermodal operations experience; configurable or low-code  
workflow products; Spanish; product investment or P&L ownership

Pay: $250,000.00 - $300,000.00 per year

Work Location: Remote

Trillium Health Partners is one of Canada’s largest community-based teaching hospitals, serving the growing and diverse populations of Mississauga, West Toronto, and surrounding communities through the Credit Valley Hospital, the Mississauga Hospital, the Queensway Health Centre, the Reactivation care Centre (Church Site) and the new THP-UHN Reactivation Care Centre. Guided by our values of compassion, excellence, and courage, and through our strategic roadmap, Plan to 2030, we are creating a new kind of health care - defined not by illness, but by the health and well-being of people and communities.

The Mississauga Halton Central West (MHCW) Regional Cancer Program (RCP) is one of 14 Regional Cancer Programs responsible for championing and influencing system transformation to drive performance of the cancer system and the region. The MHCW RCP, in alignment with Ontario Health-Cancer Care Ontario (OH-CCO), oversees the delivery and quality of cancer services for over 2 million residents across Mississauga Halton and Central West, including Etobicoke, Mississauga, Halton Hills, Oakville, Milton, Georgetown, Bolton, Brampton, Caledon, Malton, Orangeville, Rexdale, Shelburne and Woodbridge.

**Position Overview:**

As the Regional Cancer Program Director for the Mississauga Halton Central West Regional Cancer Program, you will report to the Regional Vice President. A broad and influential leadership role that includes both a regional and programmatic mandate, you will lead regional planning and performance improvement in one of the largest regional cancer programs in the province. The Regional Director leads an inter-professional team providing system and regional leadership, relationship management, performance management and financial and risk management for cancer services across the region. Cancer Services include Systemic Treatment, Radiation Therapy, Surgical Oncology, Cancer Imaging, Pathology & Lab Medicine, Prevention, Cancer Screening, Primary Care, Psycho-social Oncology, Patient Education, and Survivorship. Additionally, the role provides integration and engagement/support for the Regional Endoscopy Services, Complex Malignant Haematology, Regional Cancer Informatics and Patient Experience across 4 hospitals partners (10 hospital sites), and 34 OSBP sites.

The Regional Director, in collaboration with the Regional Vice President and in alignment with the Ontario Cancer Plan 6, will lead the delivery of strategic initiatives to ensure quality care for patients and their families, and will play a vital role in building and sustaining excellence in regional service delivery.

* Develop and implement key strategic initiatives aligned with the Ontario Cancer Plan linked with the MHCW RCP’s strategic plan, goals and objectives
* Build high performing teams that implement local and regional aspects of the Ontario Cancer Plan
* Implement the clinical quality improvement agenda of the provincial program for all cancer clinical service delivery areas
* Establish and maintain operational partnerships in the region necessary to advance cancer system performance and priorities as well as jointly develop solutions to cancer system and related challenges
* Together with the RVP, facilitate cancer service capacity planning within the Regional Cancer Program and as part of province-wide cancer planning.
* Together with the RVP, build and maintain relationships with a range of care networks, community providers and cross-sector agencies to advance a partnership strategy that is integrated and outcome-focused
* Support performance oversight of the cancer system in the region (including performance of volumes, data, access safety and quality) and lead efforts to improve regional performance
* Champion provincial cancer standards to ensure these are put into practice at the point of care, through dissemination of standards and compliance monitoring
* Support the RVP to oversee cancer related funding within the RCP, assessing existing capacity and developing strategies to optimize regional resources
* Collaborate and liaise with OH-CCO and the Regional Directors throughout the province through participation and leadership on provincial committees and projects with the goal to advance the overall care experience for persons with cancer in our community

**Qualifications:**

The successful candidate will possess the following experience, skills, attributes, and capabilities:

* Master's degree in health administration, Health Sciences, Business Administration, or related field
* Minimum 5–7 years of progressive leadership experience within a complex healthcare environment, preferably within oncology
* Experience within the Ontario cancer system and strong knowledge of regional service delivery models is considered an asset

Title: Project Manager
Description:
**Position Highlights**

**Location:** This position will work a hybrid schedule in Atlanta, GA and/or Washington, D.C. Relocation expenses are not provided. Up to 10% domestic travel may be required.

**Salary Range:** $90,000 - $105,000

**Position Type:** Grant-funded, limited-term opportunity contingent upon funding

**End Date:** September 29, 2027, with the possibility of extension.

**Overview**

The Project Manager (PM) will manage logistics, implementation, and coordination of the Newborn Essentials Support Toolkit (NEST) initiative, a federal maternal and child health program led by the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) with support from CDC Foundation. The NEST initiative provides families with essential newborn and postpartum supplies, maternal health items, and trusted information and resources at or shortly before birth. This position may also support related maternal and child health programs.

The Project Manager will draw upon expertise in logistics and maternal and child health to manage national product distribution, contracting, partnerships, data tracking systems, and other program needs. This role will coordinate vendors, distribution partners and health systems, federal partners, and other key stakeholders. The ideal candidate possesses experience managing large logistics operations, fulfillment processes, vendor relationships and multi-site distribution while ensuring compliance and sustained quality performance. Experience in maternal and child health will also enable this role to identify potential synergies and opportunities, conduct quality improvement, support evaluation efforts, and ultimately maximize program impact.

The Project Manager will work closely with internal and external partners to procure goods or services, distribute kits nationwide, onboard partner distribution sites, and manage overall implementation of the program. The Project Manager combines strong technical skills, management and leadership with an entrepreneurial and mission-driven approach to unleash the power of collaboration.

Hybrid candidates based near Atlanta, GA or Washington, D.C. are preferred. Remote work may be considered for exceptional candidates. Relocation expenses are not provided.

This role is funded through September 29, 2027, with the possibility for extension.

**Duties and Responsibilities**

* Lead and coordinate day-to-day NEST implementation across CDC Foundation teams and external partners, ensuring procurement, logistics, distribution partner onboarding, evaluation, communications, and other workstreams remain aligned and move forward on schedule.
* Oversee supply chain operations including contractor management, forecasting, inventory management, fulfillment, warehousing, shipping, and distribution.
* Lead coordination and oversight of manufacturers, suppliers, logistics vendors and distribution partners, ensuring effective onboarding, inventory management, and timely product distribution to implementation sites.
* Monitor operational and program performance, proactively identifying risks, implementing corrective actions and leading issue resolution to ensure successful delivery of program objectives.
* Serve as the primary day-to-day liaison to HHS for NEST, building a highly collaborative, responsive, and trusted working relationship with federal program leadership and reliably translating HHS priorities, decisions, and requirements into implementation.
* Build and maintain program management and data-tracking tools, including spreadsheets, dashboards, and automated workflows, to integrate information across workstreams, reduce manual processes, improve visibility, and create scalable systems as NEST grows.
* Proactively identify and solve implementation challenges, anticipating needs, developing practical solutions, exercising sound judgment, and knowing when to independently advance work, offer recommendations to CDC Foundation colleagues, or seek Federal government direction or a decision.
* Build strong working relationships and effectively coordinate without direct authority, ensuring NEST priorities are understood and advanced across relevant CDC Foundation teams, vendors, distribution partners, and other stakeholders.
* Rapidly develop and maintain fluency in the NEST program model, priority populations, maternal and infant health context, and relevant federal requirements to accurately represent the program and support sound implementation.
* Demonstrate exceptional interpersonal judgment, discretion, reliability, responsiveness, and collaborative instincts, with the ability to communicate candidly, receive and incorporate feedback, build trust quickly, and operate as a close implementation partner to senior government leadership in a fast-moving environment.
* Prepare required reports, including narrative and financial reports for private and federal funders.
* Travel as needed to represent the designated project and the CDC Foundation (up to 10 percent annually).
* Participate in and/or lead special projects and other duties as assigned.
* Other duties as assigned.

**Qualifications and Necessary Skills**

* Master's degree in public health, business administration, supply chain management, healthcare administration or a related field.
* At least 10 years of relevant professional experience, with a minimum of 5+ years of experience in maternal and child health programs and/or supply chain and logistics required. Experience in both sectors is strongly preferred.
* Experience with healthcare systems and federal funding preferred.
* Experience managing multi-state or national initiatives, preferably involving logistics, healthcare delivery, and/or maternal health support.
* Knowledgeable of inventory management, fulfillment operations, procurement processes and supply chain management.
* Experience developing and utilizing operational dashboards, performance metrics and data analytics to drive quality improvement and operational decision-making.
* Experience managing third-party vendors, distributors, manufacturers or logistics providers.
* Skilled in project management, budget management, and creative problem solving.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
* Strong technical skills including word processing, spreadsheet and database management.
* Ability to represent the CDC Foundation and its partners, leading discussions and negotiations concerning project planning, implementation and evaluation.
* Outstanding interpersonal and teamwork skills; collegial, energetic, and able to develop productive relationships with colleagues, donors and partners.
* Sound judgment and maturity, exemplified by consistent professionalism in dealing with individuals at all levels both internally and externally.

The CDC Foundation is a smoke-free environment.

We comply with all applicable laws, including E.O. 11246 and the Vietnam Era Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974 governing employment practices and do not discriminate on the basis of any unlawful criteria in accordance with 41 C.F.R. §§ 60-300.5(a)(12) and 60-741.5(a)(7).
