The CDC Foundation is an independent nonprofit authorized by Congress to mobilize philanthropic partners to support the public health system, including the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), in preventing and responding to threats to health. In this role, we are focused on one priority: building catalytic, flexible and impactful partnerships—with corporations, philanthropies, individuals and organizations—to help improve the health and lives of people in all communities, everywhere. Title: System Director of Technology Operations and Governance
Description:
Pay Range:$75.26 - $105.59 The System Director, Technology Operations & Governance provides enterprise leadership and operational accountability for technology operations, service delivery, information security operations, technology project and portfolio performance, vendor management, service management, major incident coordination, and continuous improvement. The position ensures technology services are reliable, secure, responsive, financially responsible, and aligned with organizational priorities and the needs of clinical, operational, and administrative stakeholders.
  
  
Reporting to the Chief Information Officer, the System Director leads a multidisciplinary portfolio that includes Help Desk leadership and support personnel, Information Security Operations leadership and staff, and IT Vendor Management staff. The position establishes operating standards, governance practices, performance measures, escalation paths, decision rights, and accountability across these functions.
  
  
Serves as the CIO's designated operational leader and strategic partner for enterprise technology governance, service delivery, information security operations, portfolio performance, and vendor management activities. As a senior member of the Information Technology leadership team, the position translates strategy into disciplined execution, supports executive decision-making, and provides leadership continuity for day-to-day technology operations.
  
  
SEARHC is a non-profit health consortium which serves the health interests of the residents of Southeast Alaska. We see our employees as our strongest assets. It is our priority to further their development and our organization by aiding in their professional advancement.
  
  
Working at SEARHC is more than a job, it’s a fulfilling career. We offer generous benefits, including retirement, paid time off, paid parental leave, health insurance, dental, and vision benefits, life insurance and long and short-term disability, and more.
  
  
**Key Essential Functions And Accountabilities Of The Job**
**Strategy, Executive Leadership, and CIO Partnership**

* Serve as the CIO's designated operational leader and strategic partner for enterprise technology governance, service delivery, information security operations, portfolio performance, and vendor management activities.
* Translate organizational and IT strategy into operating plans, priorities, resource requirements, performance expectations, and measurable outcomes.
* Advise the CIO and executive leadership on operational performance, information security priorities, portfolio health, vendor exposure, service capacity, and investment priorities.
* Prepare executive briefings, governance materials, business cases, risk summaries, budget recommendations, and decision requests.
* Represent Information Technology in enterprise governance forums and act on behalf of the CIO for assigned operational matters.

**Enterprise Technology Operations and Service Delivery**

* Lead enterprise technology operations and assigned service-delivery functions across all organizational locations and supported users.
* Establish IT service-management standards, operating procedures, service ownership, escalation paths, and performance expectations.
* Oversee major incident coordination, executive escalation, service restoration, root-cause review, corrective actions, and communications.
* Ensure operational readiness for implementations, upgrades, major changes, and transitions from project delivery into sustainable support.
* Maintain dashboards addressing demand, capacity, service levels, recurring issues, risks, customer experience, and improvement priorities.

**IT Service Desk and End-User Support**

* Lead Help Desk and assigned end-user support functions, ensuring timely, effective, courteous, and consistent service.
* Establish and monitor service-level expectations, customer satisfaction, first-contact resolution, backlog health, response time, resolution time, and escalation quality.
* Improve intake, triage, assignment, knowledge management, self-service, automation, communications, and request-fulfillment workflows.
* Use performance data and customer feedback to drive problem management, training, standardization, automation, and continuous improvement.

**Information Security Operations**

* Provide leadership and administrative oversight for assigned Information Security Operations personnel and security operations capabilities.
* Coordinate security monitoring, threat detection, incident response, vulnerability management, identity and access operations, security tooling, regulatory readiness, operational risk management, and performance reporting.
* Ensure information security risks, audit findings, security incidents, compliance gaps, and remediation commitments have accountable owners, target dates, documented status, and escalation.
* Provide clear, risk-based reporting to executives and governance bodies regarding security operations performance, threat activity, incident response, vulnerability exposure, regulatory readiness, remediation, and resource needs.
* Ensure information security requirements are incorporated into projects, procurements, vendor reviews, architecture decisions, operational changes, clinical workflows, and service transitions.

**IT Project and Portfolio Governance**

* Establish portfolio intake requirements for technology, evaluation, prioritization, sequencing, governance, resource planning, risk management, status reporting, change control, and closure practices.
* Ensure projects have defined sponsorship, scope, outcomes, timelines, budgets, dependencies, operational owners, readiness criteria, and benefit measures.
* Review portfolio health and intervene when technology projects face material schedule, budget, scope, resource, vendor, adoption, or operational-readiness risk.
* Coordinate technology portfolio priorities with the PMO to align with organizational strategy, regulatory commitments, operational capacity, technical roadmaps, information security requirements, and funding.

**IT Vendor, Contract, and Third-Party Governance**

* Lead governance for strategic, high-risk, and operationally significant technology vendors.
* Establish accountable ownership, performance standards, service-review cadence, scorecards, escalation processes, and corrective-action expectations.
* Coordinate technology contract planning, renewals, amendments, statements of work, licensing, support agreements, service levels, and vendor obligations.
* Monitor vendor cost, utilization, performance, support quality, regulatory posture, contractual compliance, lifecycle risk, concentration risk, and value realization.
* Maintain forward visibility into renewals, notice periods, price changes, licensing exposure, implementation commitments, and vendor dependencies.

**Financial, Workforce, and Resource Management**

* Develop and manage assigned operating and capital budgets, forecasts, staffing plans, consulting resources, and contract expenditures.
* Align staffing, vendor capacity, and project resources with demand, organizational priorities, risk, and operational commitments.
* Develop workforce plans, succession considerations, role clarity, cross-training, professional-development priorities, and recruitment strategies.
* Lead, coach, develop, and hold accountable directors, managers, professional staff, consultants, and vendor resources.

**Governance, Performance, and Continuous Improvement**

* Establish an integrated operating rhythm for service performance, information security operations, project delivery, vendor performance, budget, workforce capacity, and improvement initiatives.
* Define measurable goals and key performance indicators; use data to guide decisions and hold leaders and partners accountable.
* Ensure policies, procedures, standards, playbooks, service documentation, knowledge articles, dependency records, and escalation information are current and usable.
* Promote transparent prioritization, consistent decision-making, operational discipline, documentation, and follow-through.

**Other Functions**

**Supervisory Responsibilities**

* Provides matrixed leadership across technology teams during major incidents, enterprise projects, service transitions, vendor escalations, and material risk response.

Title: Associate Director of Programs - Wellbrook Place West
Description:
Partners Community Health (PCH) is a new not-for-profit organization, focused on bringing healthcare services together around the needs of people living in Mississauga and West Toronto. PCH currently operates two new state-of the-art LTC homes and community hub in West Mississauga. The new homes have a combined 632-beds and be part of PCH’s larger strategy that introduce innovative and inclusive programs and services and new models of care delivery. PCH is committed to building partnerships and connections that put people first, as well as a learning and leading healthcare community that provides best in class service across the aging continuum.
  
  
Position Summary
  
The Director of Programs, Long-Term Care provides strategic and operational leadership for all resident-focused programs across our long-term care home(s). Reporting to the Executive Director, the Director ensures that programs are person-centred, evidence-informed, and compliant with the Fixing Long-Term Care Act, 2021 and its regulations.
  
The Director leads a multidisciplinary team responsible for delivering high-quality programming in areas such as nursing and personal care, recreation and social engagement, rehabilitation and physiotherapy, restorative care, dementia and palliative supports, and family and community partnerships.
  
A significant component of this role is the strategic and operational oversight of the home's rehabilitation and physiotherapy programs. This includes ensuring the effective delivery of physiotherapy, rehabilitation, restorative care, and mobility services that support residents in maintaining or improving their functional abilities, independence, mobility, and overall quality of life.
  
The Director fosters a culture of dignity, safety, accountability, collaboration, and continuous quality improvement while ensuring that all programs respond to the changing needs, preferences, and goals of residents.
  
Key Responsibilities
  
1. Program Leadership and Strategy
  
  

* Develop, implement, and evaluate a comprehensive program strategy that aligns with the organization's mission, strategic plan, and resident-centred model of care.
* Oversee the planning and delivery of all resident programs, including nursing and personal care, recreation and leisure, spiritual and cultural care, restorative care, rehabilitation and physiotherapy, and palliative and end-of-life supports.
* Identify service gaps and emerging resident needs, and lead the development of new or enhanced programs in collaboration with clinical and interdisciplinary teams.
* Translate best practices, current research, and evidence-informed approaches into practical, measurable program improvements.
* Ensure programs are integrated across departments and contribute to residents' physical, emotional, social, spiritual, and psychological well-being.
* Promote innovative approaches to resident engagement, functional independence, rehabilitation, and quality of life.

2. Rehabilitation and Physiotherapy Program Oversight
  
  

* Provide strategic and operational leadership and oversight of the home's rehabilitation and physiotherapy programs, ensuring effective delivery of resident-centred rehabilitation services.
* Oversee physiotherapy, occupational therapy, restorative care, and other rehabilitation services, as applicable, ensuring programs are aligned with residents' assessed needs, individualized care plans, and functional goals.
* Ensure residents receive timely assessments, individualized treatment plans, ongoing reassessments, and appropriate rehabilitation interventions to maintain or improve mobility, strength, balance, range of motion, and functional independence.
* Monitor the quality, effectiveness, and accessibility of rehabilitation and physiotherapy services, using measurable outcomes to evaluate program performance and resident progress.
* Work collaboratively with nursing, personal support workers, recreation, dietary, and other interdisciplinary team members to integrate rehabilitation goals into residents' daily care and routines.
* Provide leadership and direction to rehabilitation and physiotherapy personnel, ensuring appropriate staffing, scheduling, performance management, and professional development.
* Oversee rehabilitation resources, equipment, service contracts, and operational processes to ensure effective and efficient program delivery.
* Ensure appropriate documentation, communication, and follow-up regarding rehabilitation assessments, treatment plans, interventions, and resident outcomes.
* Identify opportunities to enhance restorative care and rehabilitation programming, including falls prevention, mobility maintenance, functional improvement, and strategies to reduce avoidable functional decline.
* Ensure rehabilitation and physiotherapy services comply with applicable legislation, professional practice standards, Ministry of Long-Term Care requirements, and organizational policies.
* Promote ongoing education and development of staff to support safe mobility, proper transfer techniques, restorative approaches, and rehabilitation principles throughout the home.

3. Quality, Compliance, and Risk Management
  
  

* Ensure all programs comply with the Fixing Long-Term Care Act, 2021, Ontario Regulation 246/22, Ministry of Long-Term Care requirements, and other applicable legislation and standards.
* Lead required program evaluations, annual reviews, and continuous quality improvement (CQI) initiatives, tracking outcomes through key quality indicators.
* Prepare for and respond to Ministry inspections, complaints, critical incidents, and accreditation reviews, including the development and monitoring of compliance action plans.
* Oversee infection prevention and control, falls prevention, responsive behaviours, skin and wound care, pain management, rehabilitation, restorative care, and other required clinical programs.
* Monitor and evaluate rehabilitation and physiotherapy program outcomes, including resident functional improvement, mobility, falls, and maintenance of activities of daily living.
* Ensure rehabilitation and physiotherapy programs are incorporated into the home's continuous quality improvement initiatives and annual program evaluations.
* Monitor compliance with applicable professional practice standards and ensure rehabilitation services are delivered safely and in accordance with residents' individualized care plans.
* Identify, assess, and mitigate program-related risks, ensuring timely reporting, investigation, and follow-up on incidents.
* Identify and address gaps in program delivery, equipment, resources, and staffing to support quality resident outcomes.

4. People Leadership and Team Development
  
  

* Provide direct leadership, coaching, and performance support to program managers, department heads, and team leaders, fostering a respectful, collaborative, and accountable team culture.
* Provide leadership and oversight to interdisciplinary teams, including rehabilitation and physiotherapy personnel, ensuring effective communication, collaboration, and service delivery.
* Lead recruitment, onboarding, orientation, and ongoing education of program staff and volunteers.
* Support staff retention and well-being and promote a positive and psychologically safe workplace.
* Work collaboratively with union and labour relations partners where applicable, in accordance with collective agreements and organizational policies.
* Establish clear performance expectations, monitor departmental outcomes, and support professional growth and accountability.
* Encourage teamwork and collaboration across nursing, rehabilitation, recreation, and other departments to ensure coordinated resident care and services.

5. Resident, Family, and Community Engagement
  
  

* Champion residents' rights, dignity, choice, and individuality in all program planning and delivery.
* Work with the Residents' Council and Family Council to gather input, respond to concerns, and support their involvement in program development.
* Build and maintain partnerships with community agencies, health system partners, Ontario Health Teams, educational institutions, rehabilitation providers, and volunteer organizations.
* Ensure culturally safe, inclusive, and equitable programming that reflects the diversity of residents and their families.
* Promote meaningful resident and family participation in care planning, rehabilitation goals, recreation, and quality improvement initiatives.
* Support effective communication with residents and families regarding available programs, services, and opportunities for participation.

6. Financial and Operational Management
  
  

* Develop and manage program budgets, staffing models, and resources, ensuring effective use of provincial funding envelopes, including nursing and personal care, programs and support services, and other applicable funding sources.
* Oversee the operational and financial management of rehabilitation and physiotherapy programs, including staffing, equipment, contracts, supplies, and service delivery.
* Monitor expenditures and report on program performance, outcomes, and financial variances to the Executive Director and Board, as required.
* Ensure resources are allocated effectively to meet resident needs and organizational priorities.
* Prepare funding applications, reports, and reconciliations in accordance with Ministry and funder requirements.
* Monitor departmental productivity, service utilization, and performance indicators to identify opportunities for operational efficiencies and service improvements.
* Contribute to organizational planning, policy development, and senior leadership initiatives.

Qualifications
  
Required
  
  

* Bachelor's degree in nursing, gerontology, health administration, social work, rehabilitation sciences, or a related health or social services field; a master's degree is an asset.
* Current registration in good standing with the College of Nurses of Ontario or another relevant regulatory college, where applicable to the role.
* Minimum of 7 years of progressive experience in long-term care, seniors' services, or a related health care setting, including at least 3 years in a management or senior leadership role.
* Demonstrated experience in program development, operational management, quality improvement, budgeting, and change management.
* Demonstrated experience overseeing multidisciplinary programs, with experience in rehabilitation, physiotherapy, restorative care, or allied health services strongly preferred.
* Demonstrated knowledge of the Fixing Long-Term Care Act, 2021, its regulations, and Ministry of Long-Term Care inspection and compliance processes.
* Strong understanding of person-centred, trauma-informed, and palliative approaches to care, as well as dementia care and responsive behaviours.
* Knowledge of rehabilitation approaches that support mobility, functional independence, falls prevention, restorative care, and maintenance of activities of daily living.
* Experience managing teams, monitoring program outcomes, and ensuring effective use of staffing and financial resources.
* Valid Vulnerable Sector Check, up-to-date immunizations, and proof of eligibility to work in Canada.

Assets
  
  

* Certification or training in long-term care administration, gerontology, leadership, rehabilitation management, or quality improvement.
* Experience managing physiotherapy, occupational therapy, rehabilitation, or restorative care programs in a long-term care or seniors' care environment.
* Experience with interRAI/RAI-MDS, point-of-care documentation systems, and accreditation processes.
* Experience working in a unionized environment.
* Understanding of the roles and responsibilities of physiotherapists, occupational therapists, rehabilitation assistants, and restorative care teams.
* Proficiency in a second language commonly spoken in the Peel Region community.

Core Competencies
  
  

* Strategic Thinking: Sees the big picture and translates organizational vision into actionable plans and measurable outcomes.
* Collaborative Leadership: Builds trust, engages teams, and works effectively across disciplines and departments.
* Communication: Communicates clearly and compassionately with residents, families, staff, community partners, and regulators.
* Accountability and Integrity: Takes ownership of outcomes and models ethical, transparent decision-making.
* Problem Solving and Resilience: Responds calmly and effectively in a fast-paced, regulated environment.
* Equity and Cultural Humility: Promotes inclusion and respects the diverse backgrounds of residents, families, and staff.
* Operational Excellence: Demonstrates strong organizational, financial, and program management skills, with the ability to balance competing priorities.
* Quality and Innovation: Promotes continuous improvement, evidence-informed practices, and innovative approaches to resident care and rehabilitation.

Working Conditions
  
  

* Work is performed primarily on site in a long-term care home, with regular interaction with residents, families, and staff.
* Standard hours are Monday to Friday, with flexibility required for evenings, weekends, and on-call coverage during emergencies, outbreaks, or inspections.
* Occasional travel may be required for meetings, training, and community partnerships.

Equity and Accommodation Statement
  
We are committed to building a diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace. Applications are welcome from all qualified candidates, and accommodations are available upon request at any stage of the recruitment process in accordance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act, 2005 and the Ontario Human Rights Code.
  
**Salary Range:** $74,000 to $85,000
  
  
PCH is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to Equity, Diversity, Inclusion and Anti-Racism. We believe diverse and inclusive teams support strong decision making, fosters a culture of belonging and allows us to better serve our people, residents, and community. In accordance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act, 2005 and the Ontario Human Rights Code, we are committed to providing accommodations and will work with employees to meet their needs through the recruitment process. If you are a person with a disability and require assistance during the application process, please let us know. We embrace an inclusive work environment and welcome members of all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives to apply.
  
  
**To learn more about PCH, visit our website here:** https://partnerscommunityhealth.ca/
  
  
To learn more about Wellbrook Place, the new long-term care homes and seniors hub, click here: https://www.partnerscommunityhealth.ca/wellbrook-place/

Title: Director, Project Management
Description:
Everest Clinical Research (“Everest”) is a full-service contract research organization (CRO) providing a broad range of expertise-based clinical research services to worldwide pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and medical device industries. We serve some of the best-known companies and work with many of the most advanced drugs, biologics, and medical devices in development today.

Everest has been an independent CRO since 2004 with a strong foundation as a statistical and data management center of excellence. Building on this foundation, Everest has successfully developed and established itself as a full-service CRO. Everest’s Corporate headquarters are located in Ontario, Canada and US headquarters in New Jersey, USA, with additional physical offices in Asia and Europe.

Everest is known in the industry for its high-quality deliverables, superior customer service, and flexibility in meeting clients’ needs. A dynamic organization with an entrepreneurial origin, Everest continues to experience exceptional growth and great success.

Quality is our backbone, customer-focus is our tradition, flexibility is our strength…that’s us…that’s Everest.

To drive continued success in this exciting clinical research field, we are seeking a committed, skilled, and customer-focused individual to join our winning team as a **Director, Project Management** for our Toronto/Markham, Ontario, Canada on-site location, or remotely from a home-based office anywhere in Canada in accordance with our Work from Home policy.

**Director, Project Management:**

This leadership role will oversee the project planning, communication, and execution of clinical research and development services offered by Everest. Direct reports include all levels and roles within the Project Management department, including Associate Directors, Senior Managers, Managers, Senior Project Managers, Project Managers, Associate Project Managers and Project Coordinators. In-direct reports/subordinates are those Project Managers who are assigned to the tasks on the client studies and projects overseen by the Director of Project Management (matrixed organization).

**JOB ACCOUNTABILITIES:**

* Plan and implement new client service delivery requests within client portfolio; support evolution of existing client portfolio, providing holistic biometrics and full services (including clinical operations) project deliveries across multiple clinical development programs.
* Strategically align the efforts of functional area directors and managers in project planning, identification of tasks and deliverables, and assessment of resource needs and utilization for existing and new clients/sponsors.
* Perform project and portfolio performance tracking for responsible projects using strategic planning and project tracking methods and tools. Conduct regular project progress reviews with internal teams for assigned portfolios, and facilitate conduct of Everest and Client governance meetings to optimize partnership expectations and performance.
* Check and ensure that responsible projects carried out at Everest are properly tracked and managed according to Everest’s quality, operational and financial budget standards. Support solution and budget development for complex and unique projects and scope to address client requirements.
* Provide leadership, training, mentorship, and management oversight of project management staff. This may include mentorship and training of team members to deliver project management services for specific client portfolios, or mentorship and career development of individuals in a line management capacity.
* In consultation with the senior Project Management leadership, review new Project Management Applicants and recommend hires for interview processing.
* In consultation with the senior Project Management leadership, further develop and establish policies and Standard Operating Procedures in project management for assurance of quality deliverables. Continue to support the development, update, and review of governing documents and WIs for the department.
* Initiate, drive, and support project management departmental process and technology improvement initiatives. Lead and contribute to developing reusable project management templates and training materials that can be used to improve effectiveness and efficiency of project delivery by other team members.
* Through the periodic project/portfolio review meetings, effectively identify issues such as lack of planning, lack of resources, poor team performance, or other external factors negatively impacting the ongoing projects, and bring the issues and solutions to the attention of the functional area directors and managers. Work with the functional area directors and managers to jointly ensure smooth project starting up, continuation, and successful completion.
* In consultation with Everest functional leaders and senior project management leadership, interact with clients for strategic partnership governance activities, which includes but is not limited to project pipeline and delivery planning, measuring performance metrics for the portfolio, identifying new project/service opportunities within the existing portfolio, implementing performance improvement and innovation initiatives, and obtaining key information to aid in the projection of resource requirements and project management purposes.
* Manage all project management aspects of assigned Phase I -IV clinical trials and in accordance with ICH guidelines, FDA, Health Canada, EMA, and other applicable regulatory and legal requirements.
* Lead cross-functional project teams. Manage the planning, implementation, conduct, and reporting of assigned projects within the established timelines and budgets, and with the quality and requirements necessary for regulatory approvals.
* Proactively track and manage project tasks against timelines and hours spent/budgets, alert management when there are risks of having major deviations. Proactively track and manage the financial status against budget and reconcile expenses across sub-streams of activities.
* Function as senior level facilitator of problem solving and conflict resolution, and act as a 2nd level escalation resource.
* Conduct “lessons learned” meetings with project team members to learn from failures and prevent same from future projects.
* Contribute and/or participate in the performance evaluation of staff who performed under the responsible projects.
* When required, this position may assist the organization in responding to and preparing for RFI and RFPs, and subsequently leading and participating in bid defense meetings, defining work scopes and budgets, and leading contract administration activities.

**QUALIFICATIONS:**

* B.Sc. or M.Sc. in life sciences or health related field.
* A minimum of 18 years of experience in clinical research and development within a pharmaceutical, biotechnology, institutional, or CRO setting.
* Demonstrated ability to lead and develop others within functional area.
* Demonstrated understanding of cross-functional processes including clinical operations, statistics, data management, pharmacovigilance, subject randomization and drug supply management, data monitoring and adjudication committees, regulatory affairs, and medical writing.
* Knowledge and understanding of ICH guidelines, FDA, Health Canada, and EMA regulations.
* Ability to define scopes and estimate budgets, plan and manage projects, including resource requirements and utilization, hours spent vs. budgets, key deliverables and timelines.
* Demonstrated leadership abilities, including setting goals for others and driving to achieve them in accordance with allocated resources, timelines, and budgets.
* Excellent interpersonal, oral, and written communication skills. Demonstrated strong negotiation and presentation skills.
* Strong ability in problem-solving, including conflict resolution.

  

**Benefits & Compensation:**

We offer a robust benefits package to support your health, well-being, and growth, including medical, dental, and vision coverage, life & AD&D insurance, short- and long-term disability, tuition reimbursement, fitness reimbursement, employee assistance program (EAP), a pension plan, generous paid time off and sick leave, and the opportunity to earn a performance based bonus.

To find out more about Everest Clinical Research and to review other opportunities, please visit our website at www.everestclinical.com (http://www.ecrscorp.com).

--------------------------

**Preferred Qualifications**
